20.en: "That you would give your life for the God-Emperor, I have no doubt. But would you damn your soul to protect His Imperium?"

38.en: Taking up the arms of the enemy is a necessary measure of victory.

46.en: But in doing so, personal damnation and determined sacrifice are inevitable.

54.en: All Radicals are impure, lacking devotion to sacrifice, and thus must be purged.

76.en: Take the Oath of Oblation and a new name with it. Seek out the weapons of the enemy and use them to achieve victory — bind daemons, hoard forbidden knowledge, and employ damnable psykers if required. Wade into the worst heresies and sacrifice yourself to protect the Imperium.

82.en: Oblationists are damned, body and soul. They dare to use heretical weapons and powers but do not suffer others to do the same. They believe it is necessary to use the enemy’s weapons, but most mortals cannot be trusted with such power. Oblationists know they are not immune to the taint of the foul weapons and methods they employ and know they are damned for doing so, yet they make the ultimate sacrifice; it is a price worth paying to defend the Imperium with such improved strength.

86.en: The Oblationist philosophy hails from the Calixis Sector, where Inquisitor Lord Godella Morn took up daemonic weapons of the enemy to fight against the infernal forces of Chaos during the War of Brass. After her execution, some Inquisitors saw her actions as selfless rather than traitorous. Morn had damned herself to serve the Imperium, and since then, other Oblationists have done the same, not least in the Macharian Sector, wherever daemons and xenos are a constant threat.

90.en: As Radical as they come, Oblationists keep their beliefs to themselves. Many Inquisitors, especially of Puritan leanings, would execute them as tainted traitors if they knew the truth.

94.en: Yet, with their methods hidden, Oblationists can appear model Inquisitors, whether hunting xenos, battling daemons, or burning out all traces of heresy they find. While they use damned tools in their work, they are ruthless and suffer no such taint in others. They are a danger to all but the most Puritan and careful Inquisitorial agents, anyone who dares to use heretical weapons or xenostech, as well as unfortunate souls who exhibit psychic abilities or bear visible mutation.

110.en: These Inquisitors are utterly bitter characters. It is the root of Oblationism, a white-hot anger fuelled by having lost what others merely throw away, their own sacred purity.

118.en: They wield their self-corruption as if it were purity in and of itself, which they believe to be an effective justification for action against their Radical peers.

126.en: While they accept their own self-radicalism, they would never suffer the presence of another ‘lesser’ Radical; they know the Inquisition is loathfully corrupt because of them.

140.en: A Radical Inquisitor and their retinue have gone missing hunting daemon-worshipping cults near the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.1AsBzkbw2InKayw2]{Azynith Abyss}. Investigate their disappearance as dutiful acolytes should — but if they appear weakened, seize the opportunity to execute them for their heresies and purge their allies; make any necessary sacrifices to ensure the job is done. Taking over their networks and resources would be a great boon to the Oblationist Patron.

148.en: The characters' Oblationist Patron has discovered heretek activity on Hexas Panan. The forge world is already lost; the Patron is organising an assault on the planet to cleanse it — but they need a team of acolytes to secretly raid the hereteks and retrieve any useful xenotech experiments and equipment before the orbital bombardments begin.
